items.good: We have known each other for ten years.

Minho has not never eaten raw fish.

items.good: Have you ever visited Jeju Island?
bad: Did you ever visited Jeju Island?
Have you ever visit Jeju Island?
Are you ever visited Jeju Island?

cz.st: Have you ever ___ Jeju Island?

items.good: My brother has already finished his homework.
bad: My brother have already finished his homework.
My brother has already finish his homework.
My brother is already finished his homework.

cz.st: My brother ___ already finished his homework.

items.rule: 주어가 3인칭 단수(My brother)이면 현재완료는 has + 과거분사예요. already는 완료의 느낌을 더해요.

items.good: They haven't arrived yet.
bad: They hasn't arrived yet.
They haven't arrive yet.
They didn't have arrived yet.

cz.st: They ___ arrived yet.

items.rule: 부정문의 yet은 '아직'이라는 뜻이고 현재완료 haven't/hasn't + 과거분사와 함께 써요. 주어 They에는 haven't를 써요.

items.good: Has the bus left yet?
bad: Have the bus left yet?
Has the bus leave yet?
Does the bus left yet?

cz.st: ___ the bus left yet?

items.rule: 현재완료 의문문은 Has/Have + 주어 + 과거분사 ~?예요. the bus는 단수이므로 Has를 써요.

items.good: The movie has just started.
bad: The movie have just started.
The movie has just start.
The movie has just starting.

cz.st: The movie has just ___.

items.rule: just는 '방금, 막'이라는 뜻으로, have/has와 과거분사 사이에 써서 방금 일어난 일을 나타내요.

items.good: Tom has gone to Paris, so he isn't at home now.

Tom have gone to Paris, so he isn't at home now.
Tom has went to Paris, so he isn't at home now.

items.good: I have been to Japan twice.
items.ko: 나는 일본에 두 번 가 본 적이 있어요.
bad: I have be to Japan twice.
I am been to Japan twice.
I has been to Japan twice.

cz.st: I have ___ to Japan twice.

items.rule: have been to는 '~에 가 본 적이 있다'는 경험을 나타내요. be의 과거분사는 been이에요.

items.good: My uncle visited Canada last summer.
bad: My uncle has visited Canada last summer.
My uncle visit Canada last summer.
My uncle visiting Canada last summer.

cz.st: My uncle ___ Canada last summer.

items.rule: last summer처럼 과거의 특정 시점을 나타내는 말과는 현재완료가 아니라 과거 시제를 써요.

items.good: When did you buy that bike?

When are you buy that bike?

items.rule: when으로 과거의 특정 시점을 물을 때는 현재완료를 쓰지 않고 did + 동사원형을 써요.

items.good: Sora has played the violin since she was seven.
items.ko: 소라는 일곱 살 때부터 바이올린을 연주해 왔어요.
bad: Sora has played the violin since she is seven.
Sora has played the violin for she was seven.
Sora plays the violin since she was seven.

cz.st: Sora has played the violin ___ she was seven.

items.rule: since 뒤에는 시점이나 과거 시제의 절이 와요. 기간 앞에는 for를 써요.

items.good: It has rained for three days.
bad: It has rained since three days.
It has rain for three days.
It have rained for three days.

cz.st: It has rained ___ three days.

items.rule: for 뒤에는 three days 같은 기간이 와요. since 뒤에는 시작 시점이 와요.

items.good: Our team hasn't won a game this season.
items.ko: 우리 팀은 이번 시즌에 한 경기도 이기지 못했어요.
bad: Our team hasn't win a game this season.
Our team hasn't winned a game this season.
Our team doesn't won a game this season.

cz.st: Our team hasn't ___ a game this season.

items.rule: win의 과거분사는 won이에요. -ed를 붙이지 않는 불규칙 동사예요.

items.good: How long has your sister lived abroad?
items.ko: 네 언니는 외국에서 얼마나 오래 살았어요?
bad: How long has your sister live abroad?

items.good: She has drawn a picture of the lake.
bad: She has drew a picture of the lake.
She has drawed a picture of the lake.
She have drawn a picture of the lake.

cz.st: She has ___ a picture of the lake.

items.rule: draw-drew-drawn으로 변하는 불규칙 동사예요. 현재완료에는 과거분사 drawn을 써요.

items.good: The children have written letters to their grandparents.
bad: The children have wrote letters to their grandparents.
The children has written letters to their grandparents.
The children have writed letters to their grandparents.

cz.st: The children have ___ letters to their grandparents.

items.rule: write-wrote-written. have 뒤에는 과거형 wrote가 아니라 과거분사 written을 써요.

items.good: Has anyone taken my umbrella?
bad: Has anyone took my umbrella?
Have anyone taken my umbrella?
Has anyone taked my umbrella?

cz.st: Has anyone ___ my umbrella?

items.rule: take-took-taken. anyone은 단수 취급하므로 Has를 쓰고, 뒤에는 과거분사 taken을 써요.

items.good: I have never broken a bone.
items.ko: 나는 뼈가 부러진 적이 한 번도 없어요.
bad: I have never broke a bone.
I has never broken a bone.
I have never breaked a bone.

cz.st: I have never ___ a bone.

items.rule: break-broke-broken. 현재완료에는 과거분사 broken을 써요.

items.good: My grandfather has grown tomatoes in his garden for years.
items.ko: 우리 할아버지는 수년 동안 정원에서 토마토를 키워 오셨어요.
bad: My grandfather has growed tomatoes in his garden for years.
My grandfather have grown tomatoes in his garden for years.
My grandfather has grow tomatoes in his garden for years.

cz.st: My grandfather has ___ tomatoes in his garden for years.

items.rule: grow-grew-grown. 기간(for years)과 함께 쓴 현재완료에는 과거분사 grown을 써요.

items.good: My cousin has ridden a horse only once.
items.ko: 내 사촌은 말을 딱 한 번 타 봤어요.
bad: My cousin has rode a horse only once.
My cousin have ridden a horse only once.
My cousin has rided a horse only once.

cz.st: My cousin has ___ a horse only once.

items.rule: ride-rode-ridden. 경험을 나타내는 현재완료에는 ridden을 써요.

items.good: The little boy has hidden his shoes under the bed.
items.ko: 그 어린 남자아이는 침대 밑에 신발을 숨겼어요.
bad: The little boy has hided his shoes under the bed.
The little boy have hidden his shoes under the bed.
The little boy has hide his shoes under the bed.

cz.st: The little boy has ___ his shoes under the bed.

items.rule: hide-hid-hidden. 3인칭 단수 주어에는 has + hidden을 써요.

items.good: We have chosen a name for our band.
bad: We have choosed a name for our band.
We has chosen a name for our band.
We have choose a name for our band.

cz.st: We have ___ a name for our band.

items.rule: choose-chose-chosen. 규칙형 -ed를 붙인 choosed는 틀린 형태예요.

items.good: Mina has been absent since Monday.
bad: Mina has been absent for Monday.
Mina is absent since Monday.
Mina has be absent since Monday.

cz.st: Mina has ___ absent since Monday.

items.rule: 상태가 계속되는 현재완료는 has been + 형용사로 나타내고, 시작 시점(Monday) 앞에는 since를 써요.

items.good: Haven't you finished your lunch yet?
bad: Hasn't you finished your lunch yet?
Haven't you finish your lunch yet?
Don't you finished your lunch yet?

cz.st: ___ you finished your lunch yet?

items.rule: 부정 의문문도 Haven't/Hasn't + 주어 + 과거분사 ~? 순서예요. 주어 you에는 Haven't를 써요.

items.good: I have lost my wallet, so I can't pay.
bad: I have lose my wallet, so I can't pay.
I has lost my wallet, so I can't pay.
I have losed my wallet, so I can't pay.

cz.st: I have ___ my wallet, so I can't pay.

items.good: Our teacher has taught at this school for eleven years.

bad: Our teacher has taught at this school since eleven years.
Our teacher has teached at this school for eleven years.
Our teacher has teach at this school for eleven years.

cz.st: Our teacher has ___ at this school for eleven years.

items.rule: teach-taught-taught. 기간(eleven years) 앞에는 for를 써요.

items.good: My phone has stopped working.
bad: My phone has stop working.
My phone have stopped working.
My phone has stopped worked.

items.good: Nobody has answered the question yet.

cz.st: Nobody has ___ the question yet.

bad: The singer has became famous all over the world.

The singer has becomed famous all over the world.

cz.st: The singer has ___ famous all over the world.

items.good: We have been friends since elementary school.

bad: We are friends since elementary school.
We have been friends for elementary school.
We has been friends since elementary school.

cz.st: We have been friends ___ elementary school.

items.rule: since 뒤에는 시작 시점이 와요. 계속을 나타내는 현재완료와 함께 써요.

items.good: I have never heard such a funny story.

I have never hear such a funny story.
I has never heard such a funny story.

cz.st: I have never ___ such a funny story.

Many students have joinning the reading club this year.

cz.st: Many students ___ joined the reading club this year.

items.good: The scientists have discovered a new kind of fish.
bad: The scientists has discovered a new kind of fish.

items.good: Sam moved here two years ago.
bad: Sam has moved here two years ago.

items.good: It is the best pizza I have ever eaten.

bad: It is the best pizza I have ever ate.
It is the best pizza I has ever eaten.
It is the best pizza I am ever eaten.

cz.st: It is the best pizza I have ever ___.

items.rule: 최상급 뒤에 '지금까지 ~한 중에서'라는 경험은 I have ever + 과거분사로 나타내요.

items.good: Has your dog ever bitten anyone?

bad: Has your dog ever bite anyone?
Have your dog ever bitten anyone?
Did your dog ever bitten anyone?

cz.st: ___ your dog ever bitten anyone?

items.good: We haven't had a test this week.

bad: We hasn't had a test this week.
We haven't have a test this week.
We haven't has a test this week.

cz.st: We haven't ___ a test this week.

items.rule: 현재완료 부정문은 haven't/hasn't + 과거분사예요. have의 과거분사는 had예요.

items.good: She has brought her own lunch every day this week.

bad: She has bring her own lunch every day this week.
She has brang her own lunch every day this week.
She have brought her own lunch every day this week.

cz.st: She has ___ her own lunch every day this week.

items.rule: bring-brought-brought. 불규칙 동사이므로 -ed를 붙이지 않아요.

items.good: My parents have sung in a choir for many years.

bad: My parents have sang in a choir for many years.
My parents has sung in a choir for many years.
My parents have singed in a choir for many years.

cz.st: My parents have ___ in a choir for many years.

items.rule: sing-sang-sung. have 뒤에는 과거형 sang이 아니라 과거분사 sung을 써요.

items.good: He has spent all his money on games.
items.ko: 그는 게임에 돈을 다 써 버렸어요.
bad: He has spended all his money on games.
He have spent all his money on games.
He has spend all his money on games.

cz.st: He has ___ all his money on games.

items.rule: spend-spent-spent. spended라는 형태는 없어요.

items.good: The price of tickets has risen again.
bad: The price of tickets has rose again.
The price of tickets have risen again.
The price of tickets has rised again.

cz.st: The price of tickets has ___ again.

items.rule: rise-rose-risen. 주어 The price는 단수이므로 has + risen이에요.

items.good: Yuri has met her pen pal twice.

bad: Yuri has meet her pen pal twice.
Yuri has meeted her pen pal twice.
Yuri have met her pen pal twice.

cz.st: Yuri has ___ her pen pal twice.

items.rule: meet-met-met. 경험을 나타내는 현재완료에 과거분사 met을 써요.

items.q: Choose the best word: I have known Sumi ___ we were in first grade.
items.why: we were in first grade는 과거의 한 시점을 나타내는 절이므로 since를 써요. for는 기간 앞에 써요.

items.q: My grandmother has been in the hospital ___ two weeks.
items.why: two weeks는 기간이므로 for를 써요. since 뒤에는 시작 시점이 와요.

items.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: I have seen that film last night.
I have saw that film last night.
I saw that film last night.
I see that film last night.
items.why: last night은 과거의 특정 시점이므로 과거 시제를 써요. 현재완료와는 함께 쓰지 않아요.

items.q: Ann isn't here. She ___ to the post office. She will come back soon.
items.why: 지금 여기에 없고 곧 돌아온다는 뜻이므로 '가고 없다'는 has gone to를 써요. has been to는 갔다가 돌아온 경험을 나타내요.

items.q: I'm back from Busan. I ___ to Busan for the festival.
items.why: 이미 돌아왔으므로 '다녀왔다'는 have been to를 써요. 주어 I에는 have를 써요.

items.q: ___ you ever tried kimchi pancakes?
items.why: 경험을 묻는 현재완료 의문문은 Have you ever + 과거분사 ~?예요.

items.q: Sujin ___ been to a concert before.
items.why: 경험이 없음은 has never + 과거분사로 나타내요. 주어 Sujin은 3인칭 단수이므로 has를 써요.

items.q: Which sentence uses yet correctly?
o: You have called your aunt yet.
I called my aunt yet yesterday.
Have you called your aunt yet?
I have called my aunt yet.
items.why: yet은 의문문과 부정문에서 '벌써, 아직'의 뜻으로 써요. 긍정문에서는 쓰지 않아요.

items.q: A: Do you want to see this film? B: No, thanks. I have ___ seen it.
items.why: 이미 본 적이 있다는 뜻이므로 긍정문에서 '이미'를 뜻하는 already를 써요.

items.q: A: Is Dad home? B: No, he ___ home yet.
items.why: yet이 있는 부정문은 hasn't + 과거분사예요. come의 과거분사는 come이에요.

items.q: Which is the past participle of speak?
items.why: speak-spoke-spoken. 현재완료에는 spoke가 아니라 spoken을 써요.

items.q: Which line shows the correct three forms (base - past - past participle)?
items.why: take-took-taken, eat-ate-eaten, know-knew-known이 맞아요.

items.q: Which verb has the same past and past participle form?
items.why: buy-bought-bought예요. give-gave-given, begin-began-begun, drive-drove-driven은 세 형태가 모두 달라요.

items.q: Which verb has three different forms (base, past, past participle)?
items.why: sing-sang-sung은 세 형태가 모두 달라요. cut은 모두 같고, teach와 hear는 과거와 과거분사가 같아요.

items.q: 다음 중 현재완료가 쓰인 문장은?
items.why: 현재완료는 have/has + 과거분사 형태예요.

items.q: 다음 중 현재완료의 '경험'을 나타내는 문장은?
o: I have met a famous singer once.
I have just washed the dishes.
He has lived here for ten years.
She has gone to the market.
items.why: once(한 번)는 경험을 나타내요. just는 완료, for ten years는 계속, has gone은 결과를 나타내요.

items.q: 다음 중 현재완료의 '계속'을 나타내는 문장은?
o: Dad has worked at a bank since 2015.
Dad has never worked at a bank.
Dad has just left the bank.
Did Dad work at a bank?
items.why: since 2015는 과거부터 지금까지 이어지는 상태를 나타내는 계속의 표현이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 현재완료의 '완료'를 나타내는 문장은?
o: We have visited the station twice.
We have waited here for an hour.
We arrived at the station last night.
We have just arrived at the station.
items.why: just는 '방금 막 ~했다'는 완료의 뜻이에요. twice는 경험, for an hour는 계속을 나타내요.

items.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
o: She has lived here since May.
He has worked here for a year.
I have visited Rome last year.
They have gone to the park.
items.why: last year는 과거의 특정 시점이므로 현재완료와 함께 쓸 수 없어요. visited Rome last year로 고쳐야 해요.

items.q: Which sentence has a mistake?
o: I have never rode a horse.
We have known him for years.
items.why: ride의 과거분사는 rode가 아니라 ridden이에요.

items.q: A: How long have you played the piano? B: ___
items.why: How long으로 기간을 물으면 for + 기간으로 답해요.

items.q: A: When did you start learning Chinese? B: ___
items.why: 시작한 시점을 묻는 말에는 In 2022처럼 시점으로 답해요. for 뒤에는 기간이 와요.

items.q: Which question is correct?
o: How many books you have read this month?
How many books has you read this month?
How many books have you readed this month?
How many books have you read this month?
items.why: 의문사가 있는 현재완료 의문문은 의문사 + have/has + 주어 + 과거분사 순서예요. read의 과거분사는 read예요.

items.q: Which time expression is NOT used with the present perfect?
items.why: ago는 과거의 특정 시점을 나타내므로 현재완료와 함께 쓰지 않아요.

items.q: Which time word usually goes with the simple past, not the present perfect?
items.why: yesterday는 분명한 과거 시점이라 과거 시제와 쓰고, already, ever, just는 현재완료와 자주 써요.

items.q: In the present perfect, which phrase can follow for?
items.why: for 뒤에는 three hours 같은 기간이 와요. 나머지는 모두 시점을 나타내므로 for가 아니라 since와 함께 써요.

items.q: Which phrase can follow since?
items.why: since 뒤에는 last winter 같은 시점이 와요. 나머지는 기간이므로 for와 함께 써요.

items.q: Jisu moved to Ulsan in 2020 and still lives there. Which sentence describes this?
o: Jisu has lived in Ulsan in 2020.
Jisu has lived in Ulsan since 2020.
items.why: 과거부터 지금까지 계속되는 상태는 현재완료와 since + 시점으로 나타내요.

items.q: Tom lost his bike, and he still doesn't have it. Which sentence describes this?
o: Tom lost his bike since yesterday.
items.why: 과거에 잃어버려서 지금도 없는 결과는 현재완료 has lost로 나타내요.

items.q: What does 'I have lost my phone' tell us?
o: I took my phone to school today.
I don't have my phone now.
items.why: 현재완료는 과거의 일이 지금까지 영향을 미칠 때 써요. 지금도 휴대전화가 없다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Which sentence means 'Mina is not here now'?
o: Mina has never been to Daejeon.
items.why: has gone to는 '가 버리고 지금 없다'는 뜻이에요. has been to는 다녀온 경험을 나타내요.

items.q: A: Have you finished your science report? B: ___
items.why: 현재완료 의문문에는 같은 조동사로 Yes, I have.라고 답해요.

items.q: A: Has Jun ever been late for school? B: ___
items.why: Has로 물으면 No, he hasn't.로 답해요. 주어 he에는 haven't를 쓰지 않아요.

items.q: Choose the best answer: We ___ the results yet.
items.why: 주어 We에는 haven't를 쓰고 뒤에는 과거분사 received가 와요.

items.q: Which sentence is correct?
items.why: She's는 She has의 줄임말이에요. leave의 과거분사는 left예요.

items.q: 'He has never played chess.'의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
o: 그는 체스를 한 번도 해 본 적이 없다.
그는 지금 체스를 하고 있지 않다.
items.why: has never + 과거분사는 '한 번도 ~한 적이 없다'는 경험의 부정이에요.

items.q: '나는 이 노래를 세 번 들어 봤다.'를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
o: I have heard this song three times.
I heard this song three time ago.
I have hear this song three times.
I am heard this song three times.
items.why: 경험은 have + 과거분사로 나타내요. hear의 과거분사는 heard예요.

items.q: '그는 어렸을 때부터 이 마을에 살고 있다.'를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
o: He lives in this town since he was a child.
He has lived in this town for he was a child.
He have lived in this town since he was a child.
He has lived in this town since he was a child.
items.why: 어렸을 때라는 시점부터 계속되므로 has lived와 since를 써요.

items.q: Which sentence has the correct word order?
items.why: already는 보통 have와 과거분사 사이에 써요. 주어 + have + already + 과거분사 순서예요.

items.q: Last week, we ___ a school trip to Gyeongju.
items.why: Last week은 과거의 특정 시점이므로 과거형 took을 써요.

items.q: I ___ my keys. I can't open the door now.
items.why: 과거에 잃어버려서 지금 문을 열 수 없는 결과를 나타내므로 have lost를 써요.

items.q: My aunt ___ in London in 2010, but now she lives in Seoul.
items.why: in 2010은 과거의 특정 시점이고 지금은 살지 않으므로 과거형을 써요.

items.q: I ___ him at the mall an hour ago.
items.why: an hour ago는 과거의 특정 시점이므로 과거형 saw를 써요.

items.q: ___ you ever ___ a whale?
items.why: 경험을 묻는 현재완료는 Have you ever + 과거분사예요. see의 과거분사는 seen이에요.

items.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: It has been snowy for Tuesday.
It has been snowy since Tuesday.
It have been snowy since Tuesday.
items.why: Tuesday는 시작 시점이므로 since를 쓰고, 주어 It에는 has를 써요.

items.q: A: ___ has Hana lived in Incheon? B: For about eight years.
items.why: for about eight years로 답했으므로 기간을 묻는 How long이 알맞아요.

items.q: A: ___ have you been to the dentist this year? B: Only once.
items.why: Only once는 횟수에 대한 답이므로 How many times가 알맞아요.

items.q: So far, I ___ five pages of my essay.
items.why: so far(지금까지)는 현재완료와 함께 써요. 주어 I에는 have를 써요.

items.q: Which sentence is a question in the present perfect?
items.why: 현재완료 의문문은 Has/Have + 주어 + 과거분사 ~?예요.

items.q: I have lived here ___.
items.why: 현재완료의 계속에는 since last year처럼 since + 시점을 써요. 나머지는 과거 시제와 쓰는 표현이에요.

items.q: 'I haven't eaten anything since breakfast.'의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
o: 나는 아침 이후로 아무것도 먹지 않았다.
나는 아침에 아무것도 먹지 않을 것이다.
items.why: since breakfast는 '아침 식사 이후로'라는 뜻이고, haven't eaten은 지금까지 먹지 않았음을 나타내요.

items.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Did you ever have ridden a camel?
Have you ever ridden a camel?
You have ever ridden a camel.
Ever have you ridden a camel.
items.why: 경험을 묻는 질문은 Have you ever + 과거분사 ~?예요.

items.q: Which sentence uses just correctly?
items.why: just는 has와 과거분사 사이에 써요. ring의 과거분사는 rung이에요.

items.q: Mia says, 'I have never been abroad.' What do we know?
o: Mia has not traveled to another country.
items.why: have never been abroad는 외국에 한 번도 가 본 적이 없다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: Dad ___ the dishes yet, so the sink is still full.
items.why: yet이 있는 부정문이므로 hasn't + 과거분사예요. 주어 Dad에는 hasn't를 써요.

items.title: A New Hobby
items.text: Ha-eun has been interested in photography since last spring. Her uncle gave her an old camera for her birthday, and she has taken more than five hundred pictures with it. She has photographed flowers, buildings, and even her neighbor's dog. Last month she showed her best photos at a school event, and many students asked her for tips. However, she has never taken a lesson. She learns from videos online. Next year she hopes to join the photography club, which has existed for ten years.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to buy a cheap old camera
Her uncle's job as a photographer
qs.why: 글 전체가 하은이의 사진 취미를 다루고 있어요.

qs.q: Since when has Ha-eun been interested in photography?
qs.why: 첫 문장에서 since last spring이라고 했어요.

qs.q: How many pictures has Ha-eun taken with the old camera?
qs.why: she has taken more than five hundred pictures with it라고 했어요.

qs.q: The word "tips" in the passage is closest in meaning to ___.
qs.why: 사진을 어떻게 찍는지 알려 달라는 맥락이므로 '유용한 조언'이에요.

qs.q: What can we infer from the passage?
o: Ha-eun's uncle teaches her every week.
Ha-eun is learning photography mostly by herself.
Ha-eun is a member of the photography club now.
Ha-eun does not like taking pictures of animals.
qs.why: 수업을 들은 적이 없고 영상으로 배운다고 했으므로 혼자 배우고 있어요.

items.title: An Email to Grandma
items.text: Dear Grandma, How are you? I have been very busy since school started. I have joined the chess club, and I have already played in two small contests. I have won one of them! Mom has baked cookies for you, and I have helped her. I haven't visited you for a month, so I miss you a lot. Dad says we can come to your house next weekend. Have you finished the sweater you were knitting? I hope it is not too big for me! Love, Jun

qs.q: Why did Jun write this email?
o: To invite Grandma to join the chess club
To thank Grandma for a new sweater
To share his news and say hello
To say that he is sick
qs.why: 준이는 근황을 전하고 안부를 묻기 위해 이메일을 썼어요.

qs.q: How many contests has Jun won?
qs.why: 두 번 대회에 나가 그중 하나에서 이겼다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does Jun miss Grandma?
o: He hasn't visited her for a month.
She moved to another city far away.
She is in the hospital this week.
She forgot to send him a present.
qs.why: 한 달 동안 찾아뵙지 못해서 보고 싶다고 했어요.

qs.q: What will probably happen next weekend?
o: Jun will play in a chess contest.
qs.why: 아빠가 다음 주말에 할머니 댁에 갈 수 있다고 했어요.

qs.q: What can we infer about Grandma?
o: She lives in the same house as Jun.
She is making a sweater for Jun.
qs.why: 할머니가 뜨고 있던 스웨터를 다 끝냈는지 묻는 것으로 보아 준이를 위해 뜨고 있다고 짐작할 수 있어요.

items.title: Nugget the Hamster
items.text: Our class has had a pet hamster since March. His name is Nugget. Students have taken turns feeding him, and so far nobody has forgotten. Last week, however, Nugget disappeared from his cage. We have searched the whole room, and Mr. Park has even looked behind the bookshelves. At last, Yuna found him sleeping in a teacher's slipper! Now we have put a small lock on the cage, so he cannot escape again. Everyone is happy, and Nugget seems to be happy, too.

qs.q: Where did Yuna find Nugget?
qs.why: 유나가 선생님의 슬리퍼 안에서 자고 있는 너겟을 찾았어요.

qs.q: Why have the students put a lock on the cage?
o: To keep other students away from him
To make Nugget sleep during class
To stop Nugget from escaping again
To hide Nugget from the teachers
qs.why: 잠금장치를 달아 다시 도망치지 못하게 했다고 했어요.

qs.q: What is true about feeding Nugget?
o: Nobody has forgotten to feed him so far.
Students stopped feeding him last week.
qs.why: 학생들이 돌아가며 먹이를 주었고 지금까지 잊은 사람이 없다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "escape" is closest in meaning to ___.
qs.why: 우리에서 빠져나가 도망친다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Sleep and Students
items.text: Doctors have said for many years that sleep is very important for teenagers. Studies have shown that students need eight to ten hours of sleep every night. However, many students have started to use their phones late at night, and they have become more tired in class. Some schools have changed their start time to a little later, and the results have been good. Students in those schools have paid more attention and have felt happier. Experts say that a regular bedtime has helped many young people to stay healthy.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Enough sleep is important for teenagers.
Phones are the best way to study.
Schools should never change their start time.
qs.why: 글 전체가 청소년에게 충분한 수면이 중요하다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: How much sleep do students need, according to the studies?
qs.why: 연구에 따르면 매일 밤 8~10시간의 수면이 필요하다고 했어요.

qs.q: What happened in schools that started later?
o: Students stopped using their phones completely.
Teachers became more tired during class.
Students paid more attention and felt happier.
Students got less sleep than they did before.
qs.why: 수업 시작 시간을 늦춘 학교의 학생들은 더 집중하고 더 행복해졌다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "regular" in "a regular bedtime" means ___.
qs.why: regular bedtime은 매일 같은 시간에 자는 습관을 뜻해요.

items.title: Our Town Has Changed
items.text: Our town has changed a lot in the past five years. The city has built three new parks, and volunteers have planted hundreds of trees. Recycling has become part of daily life: families have separated paper, plastic, and glass since 2021. As a result, the amount of garbage has fallen by twenty percent. The river, which looked dirty for a long time, has become clean enough for fish to return. Still, the mayor says the work has not finished. She hopes more people will walk or ride bikes instead of driving.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A plan to build a new airport nearby
Good changes in a town over five years
Why so many people moved out of the town
The history of the town's old river
qs.why: 공원, 재활용, 강 등 마을이 5년간 좋게 변한 내용이에요.

qs.q: What has happened to the amount of garbage?
o: It has fallen by twenty percent.
It has risen by twenty percent.
qs.why: 재활용의 결과로 쓰레기 양이 20퍼센트 줄었다고 했어요.

qs.q: What sign shows that the river is cleaner?
o: People have built a bridge over it.
Trees have been planted beside it.
qs.why: 강이 깨끗해져 물고기가 돌아올 수 있게 되었다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does the mayor hope for?
o: More cars will use the river road.
More people will walk or ride bikes.
qs.why: 시장은 사람들이 운전 대신 걷거나 자전거를 타기를 바란다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does "the work has not finished" suggest?
o: The town has decided to stop making changes.
The town wants to make more improvements.
All of the town's problems are now solved.
The mayor is planning to leave her job soon.
qs.why: 아직 일이 끝나지 않았다는 것은 더 개선하려는 계획이 남아 있다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Gyeongju Diary
items.text: Saturday, May 10. Today we arrived in Gyeongju. We have visited two temples so far, and we have walked about ten kilometers. My legs are tired, but I haven't felt bored once. In the morning, we climbed a hill and watched the sunrise. I have never seen such a beautiful sky. Tomorrow we will visit a museum. I haven't bought any souvenirs yet, so I will do that after lunch. Our guide has promised to show us an old royal garden, too. I can't wait!

qs.q: What did the writer do in the morning?
o: Visited an art museum in the town
Bought souvenirs at a night market
Climbed a hill to see the sunrise
Had lunch in an old royal garden
qs.why: 오늘 아침에 언덕에 올라 일출을 봤다고 했어요.

qs.q: What has the writer NOT done yet?
qs.why: I haven't bought any souvenirs yet이라고 했어요.

qs.q: How does the writer feel?
qs.why: 다리는 피곤하지만 지루하지 않았고 내일을 기대하고 있어요.

qs.q: What has the guide promised?
o: To buy souvenirs for the students
To show them an old royal garden
To take them to a beach
To give them a free day
qs.why: Our guide has promised to show us an old royal garden이라고 했어요.

items.title: The Old Clock Tower
items.text: The clock tower in our town square has stood there since 1925. It has survived storms, a fire, and two big floods. Workers have repaired it three times, and each time the clock has started ticking again. Many visitors have taken pictures of it, and some have even written songs about it. Last year the town painted the tower white. Local people say the tower has become a symbol of their town. For them, it has never been just a clock.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Old clocks should be repaired every year.
Visitors do not like the old clock tower.
The town square was built just last year.
The clock tower is a symbol of their town.
qs.why: 시계탑이 오랫동안 마을의 상징이 되어 왔다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: How many times have workers repaired the tower?
qs.why: Workers have repaired it three times라고 했어요.

qs.q: What did the town do last year?
qs.why: Last year the town painted the tower white라고 했어요.

qs.q: What does "it has never been just a clock" mean?
o: It means more than a clock to people.
It has never told the correct time.
It was always broken and never worked.
It is a very small clock in a shop.
qs.why: 그냥 시계가 아니라 마을 사람들에게 더 큰 의미가 있다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Packing for Camp
items.text:
Mom: Have you packed your bag yet, Jiho?
Jiho: Not yet. I have only packed my clothes.
Mom: Have you remembered your toothbrush?
Jiho: Oh no, I haven't! Thanks for reminding me.
Mom: And have you found your flashlight? You lost it last month.
Jiho: Yes, I found it under my bed yesterday.
Mom: Great. Has Dad called the bus company?
Jiho: He has already called them. The bus leaves at seven.
Mom: Then you should go to bed early tonight.

qs.q: What has Jiho packed so far?
qs.why: I have only packed my clothes라고 했어요.

qs.q: When did Jiho find his flashlight?
qs.why: 지호는 어제 침대 밑에서 손전등을 찾았다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does Mom tell Jiho to go to bed early?
o: He has a bad cold today.
qs.why: 버스가 7시에 떠나므로 일찍 자라고 한 거예요.

qs.q: Who has already called the bus company?
qs.why: Has Dad called ...? 질문에 He has already called them이라고 답했어요.

items.title: Movie Night
items.text:
Ella: Have you ever seen a movie about space, Tae?
Tae: Yes, I have. I saw one last winter with my cousin.
Ella: Did you like it?
Tae: Very much. I have watched it twice since then.
Ella: I have never watched a space movie. Is it scary?
Tae: Not at all. It is funny and exciting.
Ella: Then let's watch it tonight. Have you finished your homework?
Tae: Not yet, but I will do it after dinner.
Ella: Okay. I will bring some popcorn.

qs.q: After he first saw the movie last winter, how many more times has Tae watched it?
qs.why: 태이는 지난겨울에 처음 봤고 그 뒤로 두 번 더 봤다고 했어요.

qs.q: What is true about Ella?
o: She has never seen a space movie.
She has watched it twice with Tae.
She saw it with Tae last winter.
qs.why: 엘라는 우주 영화를 본 적이 없다고 했어요.

qs.q: What is the movie like, according to Tae?
qs.why: 태이는 영화가 재미있고 신난다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does Ella ask about Tae's homework?
o: She wants to help him finish it tonight.
She has already finished it for him.
She wants to know if he is free tonight.
She thinks it is too difficult for him.

items.title: At the Lost and Found
items.text:
Student: Excuse me. I have lost my blue umbrella.
Teacher: When did you lose it?
Student: I think I left it in the cafeteria on Monday. I have looked for it everywhere since then.
Teacher: Have you checked the library?
Student: Yes, I have. It isn't there.
Teacher: Let me see. Someone has brought in a red one and a black one, but no blue one.
Student: Oh, that's too bad.
Teacher: Don't worry. I will tell the cafeteria staff. Please come back on Friday.
Student: Thank you very much.

qs.q: Where does the student think he left his umbrella?
qs.why: 월요일에 구내식당에 두고 온 것 같다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which place has the student already checked?
qs.why: Have you checked the library? 질문에 Yes, I have라고 답했어요.

qs.q: What umbrellas has someone brought in?
o: A red one and a black one
A blue one and a red one
qs.why: 빨간 우산과 검은 우산이 들어왔지만 파란 우산은 없다고 했어요.

qs.q: What will the teacher do?
qs.why: 선생님은 구내식당 직원에게 알리겠다고 했어요.
